stories.title: D11 Bond Election Day — COS Voters Decide $775M for School Buildings Today

x_posts.label: Post 1
x_posts.text: Today is Election Day. D11's $775M bond (Issue 4A) is on the ballot — new Holmes Middle School, HVAC at every school, high school upgrades. Drop boxes close 7 PM tonight. Find a drop box: d11.org/bond #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Today is the day COS — D11's $775 million bond is on the ballot, and polls are open right now.

Here's what's at stake for families: a new Holmes Middle School, HVAC repairs at every D11 school, upgrades at Palmer High and Coronado High, and library renovations across the district. This is the first D11 capital bond since 2004. A similar bond failed in 2021 by just 11 votes.

If it passes, the average homeowner would pay about $22 more per month on property taxes. If it fails, the district continues patching aging buildings with existing funding.

Still haven't returned your mail-in ballot? Drop boxes close tonight at 7 PM. You can find the closest drop box at d11.org/bond. D20 families, you have a bond on the ballot today too — check your district's website.

This one's close enough that every vote counts. Are you voting yes or no today?

---

stories.title: Colorado Flu Season Update — First Pediatric Death Confirmed, Vaccines Available Now

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text: Colorado confirmed the first child flu death of 2026-27 season. Child was unvaccinated. Last year: 8 kids died, 1,169 hospitalized — a state record. Flu peaks Dec-Jan. Get vaccinated now. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Colorado health officials have confirmed the first child flu death of the 2026-27 season. The child was elementary school age and had not received this year's flu vaccine.

We know this is hard to read. It's also information that matters.

Last season was Colorado's worst on record for children: 8 kids died and 1,169 were hospitalized — more than any year since the state started tracking. The 2026-27 season is starting earlier than last year. Flu typically peaks in December and January, which means we're heading into the highest-risk window right now.

The good news: it's not too late. The AAP recommends the annual flu shot for every child 6 months and older, and doses are available at most COS pharmacies and pediatric clinics. If your kids haven't gotten their flu shots yet, this week is a good time.

Families whose kids have respiratory illness symptoms — fever, cough, body aches — should call their pediatrician before heading in. Testing is available.

Have your kids gotten their flu shots yet this season?

---

stories.title: CPSC Recall Alert — Children's Bed Rails and Light-Up Toys to Check Now

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: CPSC recall: children's bed rails recalled or flagged as stop-use — HOMEAL, WYBITNY, KOOLDOO, Famill. Sold on Amazon. Entrapment/asphyxiation risk. Also: ZMC light-up toy recall (battery ingestion). Check cpsc.gov. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
If you've bought children's bed rails or light-up kids' toys from Amazon in the past year or two, take a minute to check this.

The Consumer Product Safety Commission has issued formal recalls for two brands of children's portable bed rails — HOMEAL and WYBITNY — due to a risk of entrapment and asphyxiation. Three other brands (KOOLDOO, Famill, and Yulong Tengfei) have received urgent stop-use warnings for the same hazard. All of these products were sold through Amazon.

Separately, ZMC Group has expanded a recall on light-up children's toys over a battery ingestion risk. These toys have small, powerful batteries that can cause serious internal injuries if swallowed.

What to do: stop using any recalled product immediately. Don't donate it — it may harm another family. Check cpsc.gov for the specific recall number and remedy options (refund, replacement). You can also search your Amazon order history by brand name. CPSC's hotline is 1-800-638-2772.

Is there a recall here you weren't aware of?

---

stories.title: Veterans Day Weekend Guide for COS Families — Parade, 5K, and Free Museum Entry

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: Veterans Day weekend in COS for families: free parade Sat Nov 7 (11 AM, Tejon St.), kids 5K Sun Nov 8 (9 AM, $15), ANA Money Museum free for kids 12 & under. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Veterans Day weekend is coming up, and Colorado Springs has a few good options for families who want to get out and mark the occasion.

On Saturday, November 7, the In Their Honor Veterans Day Parade kicks off at 11 AM in downtown COS, marching south down Tejon Street. It's free, it's family-friendly, and it's a meaningful hour for kids who are old enough to ask why we honor veterans.

On Sunday, November 8, the Colorado Springs Veterans Day 5K runs from 9 to 11 AM. There's a kids race for ages 15 and under — registration is $15.

If you want to add an indoor stop, the ANA Money Museum at 818 N. Cascade Ave. offers free admission for children 12 and under. They have exhibits on coins and currency history that are surprisingly kid-friendly.

This is one of those weekends where Colorado Springs' deep military roots show up in a tangible way. It's a good opportunity to talk with kids about what service means and who in their community has served.

What are your Veterans Day weekend plans?

---
